items.title: Xaluritamig Trial in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1 trial is testing xaluritamig, a new drug, in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). The main goal is to determine if the drug is safe and what side effects it may cause. This is an early-stage trial to find the right dose for future studies.

items.title: Xaluritamig Combined With Hormone Therapy for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1 study tests xaluritamig combined with hormone drugs (darolutamide or abiraterone) in patients with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. Researchers are checking if the combination is safe and tolerable. The trial is recruiting patients now.

items.title: RECIPROCAL Trial: Testing Different Dosing Schedules for Lutetium-177 PSMA
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial examines whether spacing out doses of lutetium-177 PSMA (Pluvicto) can improve quality of life without shortening survival in advanced prostate cancer patients. The standard treatment gives the drug at fixed intervals; this study tests a personalized approach. This is important research on an FDA-approved drug.

items.title: AMO959 Combined With Lutetium-177 PSMA and Hormone Therapy
items.summary: This Phase 1b/2 trial tests AMO959 combined with lutetium-177 PSMA and androgen receptor inhibitors in mCRPC patients who failed one prior hormone therapy. The study evaluates safety in Phase 1b and effectiveness in Phase 2. Patients must be PSMA-positive and some cannot have had prior chemotherapy.

items.title: ASPIRE Trial: Adding Chemotherapy to Hormone Therapy for Metastatic Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial compares adding docetaxel chemotherapy to standard hormone therapy (ADT) plus apalutamide versus hormone therapy and apalutamide alone in newly metastatic prostate cancer. The study tests whether adding chemotherapy upfront improves outcomes. This is an important trial for newly diagnosed metastatic patients.

items.title: IDeate-Prostate02: Ifinatamab Deruxtecan for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1/2 trial studies ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd) alone or combined with other treatments for mCRPC. Researchers are testing safety, finding the right dose, and measuring PSA response. I-DXd is an antibody-drug conjugate that delivers chemotherapy directly to cancer cells.

items.title: Darolutamide Maintenance Therapy in Pretreated Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial tests darolutamide maintenance therapy in mCRPC patients who already received hormone therapy and other treatments. Previous research showed darolutamide can delay cancer progression in this setting. The study examines if continuing treatment helps patients who responded to prior therapies.

items.title: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial tests whether adding mevrometostat (PF-06821497) to enzalutamide works better than enzalutamide alone in mCRPC patients who haven't received androgen receptor inhibitors yet. Mevrometostat is an investigational drug that blocks a protein involved in cancer growth. This is a large pivotal trial.

items.title: Sipuleucel-T Combined With Bipolar Androgen Therapy in mCRPC
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial combines sipuleucel-T (Provenge) immunotherapy with bipolar androgen therapy in mCRPC patients. The study measures immune response and tests whether alternating between very high and very low testosterone levels can enhance the vaccine's effectiveness. This is a novel combination approach.

items.title: VECTRA-01: AZD2265 Versus Standard Care in PSMA-Positive mCRPC
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial compares AZD2265 to standard treatments in PSMA-positive mCRPC patients. The study measures time until cancer progression on imaging and overall survival. AZD2265 is an investigational radioligand therapy similar to lutetium-177 PSMA. This is a major comparative trial.

items.title: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide for Metastatic Castration-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial tests mevrometostat combined with enzalutamide versus enzalutamide alone in newly metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer patients who haven't received hormone pills or chemotherapy yet. This tests whether adding mevrometostat earlier in treatment improves outcomes. Major trial for earlier-stage metastatic disease.

items.title: BPX-601 CAR T-Cell Therapy for Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1 trial tests BPX-601, a CAR T-cell therapy made from patients' own immune cells that are modified to attack prostate cancer. The study evaluates safety, best dose, and whether it can destroy cancer cells. This represents a novel immunotherapy approach for treatment-resistant prostate cancer.

items.title: XL092 for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial tests XL092, an oral medication taken daily, in mCRPC patients. Researchers measure how well the drug controls cancer after 16 weeks and monitor safety. XL092 is an investigational targeted therapy that blocks pathways cancer cells use to grow.

items.title: Inflammation Pathways Drive Treatment Resistance in Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This research review explains how chronic inflammation helps prostate cancer progress and resist treatment. NFκB and IL-6/JAK/STAT3 inflammatory pathways work with androgen receptors to promote tumor growth, spread, and resistance to hormone therapy. Understanding these pathways may lead to new treatment combinations targeting inflammation.

items.title: PSMA DNA Vaccine Enhances Immunotherapy Response in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This preclinical study developed a nanoplasmid DNA vaccine targeting PSMA that stimulates the immune system to fight prostate cancer. When combined with PD-1 checkpoint inhibitors, the vaccine prevented tumors and lung metastases in animal models. This approach could make immunotherapy work better in prostate cancer, which typically doesn't respond well to checkpoint inhibitors alone.

items.title: Metformin Reduces Kidney Radiation Dose During Lutetium-177 PSMA Therapy
items.source: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
items.summary: This study found that metformin (a diabetes drug) reduces radiation dose to kidneys in patients receiving lutetium-177 PSMA therapy without affecting tumor treatment. This could help protect kidney function during this treatment. The finding is important for reducing side effects while maintaining cancer treatment effectiveness.

items.title: Managing Heart Problems From Prostate Cancer Treatments
items.summary: This review discusses cardiovascular side effects of prostate cancer treatments including hormone therapy, chemotherapy, and newer drugs. Heart disease is common in prostate cancer patients and a major cause of death. The article provides strategies for preventing and managing heart complications during cancer treatment.

items.title: PARP Inhibitor Plus Immune Therapy Shows Promise in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This preclinical study combined a PARP inhibitor (olaparib) with a novel T-cell activating antibody therapy in prostate cancer models. The combination activated the immune system, shrank tumors, and improved survival. This approach could help overcome prostate cancer's resistance to immunotherapy by combining DNA damage and immune activation.

items.title: Patient Quality of Life With Radium-223 and Olaparib Combination
items.summary: The COMRADE trial showed olaparib plus radium-223 improved progression-free survival in mCRPC patients with bone metastases. This analysis examined patient-reported quality of life and pain during treatment. Understanding how treatments affect daily life helps patients and doctors make informed decisions about therapy options.
